title: Spinning
prompt: Play around with spinning. We can make spinners. We can spin things.

title: Hack a Magazine with Octostudio
prompt: Take a magazine and combine it with OctoStudio to create something magical.
description: Following the Tinkering Studio's Hack a Magazine prompt: What treasures, stories, and surprises are hiding in the pages of magazines? Take a magazine and combine it with OctoStudio to create something magical. Embed your device inside a magazine to bring static pages to life.

title: Making & Tinkering as a pathway for Ambiguity Tolerance
prompt: Use your materials to create a way for your figure to get from Here to There. Your figure is "Here" and you need to get it "There."
description: Activities and discussions inspired in part by Navigating Ambiguity: Creating Opportunity in a World of Unknowns, by Andrea Small & Kelly Schmutte.

title: Tinkering with Zip Ties
prompt: This activity is meant to be a tinkering activity where we learn more about how we can use zip ties: make something that is ambitious, make something that is useful, make something that consists mostly of zip-ties.

title: Scratch 10 Blocks
prompt: What can you create with only 10 Scratch Blocks?
description: 10 Blocks is an introduction to Scratch programming activity from the HGSE Creative Computing Lab. We tried the activity, and talked about what makes a good (intro) activity or prompt for a new topic.

title: Weave It
prompt: Explore weaving as an accessible making activity.
description: Weaving is a simple, accessible activity that can use very complicated & specialized tools or just cardboard and yarn. It can be treated as a traditional craft/artform, or taken in non-traditional ways. At in-person hub locations, we had the opportunity to try out Hello! Looms — laser cut looms created by UW-Madison Design Studies professor Marianne Fairbanks.

title: Octostudio Kaleidoscope
prompt: Let's explore a new, accessible coding tool by exploring movement, symmetry, and reflection.
description: We used the pattern exploration resources from the Exploratorium as a jumping off point to use the mobile/tablet programming tool Octostudio. In-person hubs had mirror material they could use to create kaleidoscopes to use with their code.

title: Trash Boats for the Bubbler Regatta
prompt: Create a boat that is wind powered.
description: Carve or construct small foam boats from recycled materials, styrofoam, or pool noodles. Use dowels or skewers to create masts and sails (you may have to provide your own wind!). Add ballast through decoration or pennies and see if you can get your boat to float or sail in a pool or rain gutter course.

title: Art & Motion
prompt: How can we make art with motion? How can we make art making machines?
description: Bill & Tori gave us a tour of their prototyping space at Betty Brinn, where they were exploring using salad spinners to make spin art, motors to move brushes, and black light for a seasonal touch. They invited us into their prototyping process and we explored making art with magnets, marbles, salad spinners, and more.

title: Threads and Things
prompt: How can we use textiles to tell a story?

title: Pliers and Wires
prompt: Create a one-line drawing and then build it with wire.
description: Extension: use dowels, string, and flashlights for shadow play.
materials: Wire (16 gauge or higher depending on age/project — higher gauge is thinner)
2 pairs of pliers (needle nose and small locking vice work best; vary sizes for participants)
